analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only, with no code, config or mode changes. docs/provider/direct-mode.md (head lines 130, 134, 157-181) now documents Responses continuation and retention for the local OpenAI endpoint. It describes previous_response_id handling, a bounded in-memory history store (256 responses, 64 MiB), an unbounded SDK response-object store retrievable by GET, and store:false semantics. It also adds a pointer to prefix_cache_status in /metrics. docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md (head lines 21-33) adds GLM-5.3-Flash hardware gating (M5 Max/Ultra, 256 GB, glm5_next_v1, apple_m5, mlx_nax). Both files relate to threat-model areas only indirectly: A-001 for local prompt retention, and T-041 / TB-007 for the cache metrics reference. The docs add no new network surface and do not weaken a documented control.

I noted the following without reporting a finding. Documented local retention of prompts and responses in process memory, including a GET store with no eviction, is a property of code outside this PR. The docs cover it honestly, and the local endpoint is token-authenticated by default (LocalAuthResponder, direct-mode.md lines 109-115). The `--no-auth` mode and the unauthenticated /health endpoint are pre-existing. The claimed behavior (400 on unknown ID, byte caps) cannot be verified from the supplied evidence because the source files were not provided. A later pass could check the claims against LocalResponseConversationStore and InMemoryResponseStore if a doc-code mismatch matters. No threat-model update is needed.
